# nish/cli-flags

A command line's flags, declared once as data and read back by name, with the same declaration writing the `--help` rows.

```ts
import {
  CommandSpec,
  FLAG_BOOLEAN,
  FLAG_ERR_BOOLEAN_VALUE,
  FLAG_ERR_MISSING_VALUE,
  FLAG_ERR_NOT_A_NUMBER,
  FLAG_ERR_REPEATED,
  FLAG_ERR_UNKNOWN,
  FLAG_ERR_UNKNOWN_COMMAND,
  FLAG_NUMBER,
  FLAG_OK,
  FLAG_REPEATABLE,
  FLAG_STRING,
  FlagSpec,
  FlagTable,
  ParsedFlags,
} from "nish/cli-flags";
```

```ts
import { FlagTable } from "nish/cli-flags";

const flags = new FlagTable("git-lite");
flags.command("remote add", "<name> <url>", "add a remote");
flags.string("output", "<file>", "where to write");
flags.number("jobs", "<n>", "parallel jobs");
flags.boolean("verbose", "say more");
flags.repeatable("include", "<dir>", "search here too");
const got = flags.parseFrom(process.argv, 1);
if (!got.ok) { got.exitUsage(); }
got.command;                      // "remote add", or "" for none
got.str("output"); got.num("jobs"); got.bool("verbose"); got.all("include");
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="CommandSpec" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#commandspec">

One declared command: its `path` as the words a person types, those words split once so that matching does not split them per parse, and its help.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="FlagTable" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#flagtable">

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-detail title="No function values">

A flag is a name, a kind, a placeholder and a line
of help, and the program asks the parse for a value by name afterwards, so
the table is plain data the help menu can read too (`writeHelp`).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The grammar">

**The grammar** is the GNU long-option one without the short options:
`--name value` and `--name=value` for a string, number or repeatable flag,
`--name` and `--no-name` for a boolean, `--` ending the flags, and a lone
`-` an ordinary word. Words that are not flags may come before, between or
after them; the leading ones choose the command, the longest declared path
they spell, and the rest are positionals. A flag belongs to the whole table,
not to one command: a program that wants `--force` only under `remote add`
checks `command` itself.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A usage error is an answer, not a panic">

`parse` stops at the first one
and the result carries it as data (`code`, `message`, `argument`), so a
program can test it or word it its own way; `exitUsage` is the usual
ending, the message on stderr and exit status 2, the convention `nish`
itself keeps. Asking for a flag the table does not declare, or as the wrong
kind, is a bug in the program rather than in its command line, and panics.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What it reaches">

Nothing but `exitUsage`, which reaches `exit`.

</scalar-detail>

## FlagTable

The flags and commands of one program, declared in the order its help
lists them. Each declaring method panics on a name no command line could
match (empty, a leading `-`, an `=` or whitespace in a flag name), one
declared twice, or a `no-x` beside a boolean `x`, because the table is the
program's own text and a mistake there is a bug.

```ts
class FlagTable
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new FlagTable(program: string)` |  |
| `commands: CommandSpec[]` |  |
| `flags: FlagSpec[]` |  |
| `program: string` |  |
| `boolean(name: string, description: string): void` | A boolean flag: `--name` sets it, `--no-name` clears it, once. |
| `command(path: string, shape: string, description: string): void` | A command: `path` is one or more words (`"remote add"`), `shape` what follows them in the help (`"<name> <url>"`, may be empty). Declaring any command makes leading words that spell none a usage error. |
| `declare(name: string, kind: i32, meta: string, description: string): void` | A flag of `kind`, after the checks every declaring method shares. |
| `indexOf(name: string): i32` | The index of the flag `name` (without `--`), or `-1`. |
| `matchCommand(words: string[]): i32` | The index of the command `words` spell the longest declared path of, or `-1`. A path spelled by a prefix of `words` counts; the words after it are the positionals. |
| `number(name: string, meta: string, description: string): void` | A number flag, read as an `f64`: a finite decimal (`-2.5`, `1e3`, `.5`), the same on every target. Hex, binary, `Infinity`, padding and `""` are usage errors. |
| `parse(args: string[]): ParsedFlags` | `args` read against the table, every one of them an argument: `parseFrom(args, 0)`. |
| `parseFrom(args: string[], first: i32): ParsedFlags` | `args` from index `first` on read against the table, so that a program passes `process.argv` and `1` to skip its own path. Stops at the first usage error, which the answer then carries; the command is still matched on the words read before it, so the usage hint can name it. |
| `repeatable(name: string, meta: string, description: string): void` | A flag given any number of times, each with a value. |
| `string(name: string, meta: string, description: string): void` | A string flag: `--name value` or `--name=value`, once. |
| `unknownCommand(words: string[]): string` | The words an unknown command is reported as: the leading words up to and including the first that no declared path continues with, so `remote rename x` against `remote add` is `"remote rename"`. |
| `writeHelp(menu: HelpMenu): void` | The table as help rows: a `Commands` section when any command is declared (its path, shape and description), then a `Flags` section, each in declaration order. The menu's header and usage lines are the caller's, written before this. |

## ParsedFlags

What `parse` answered: a usage error, or every flag's value. Values sit in
arrays parallel to the table's `flags`: `counts` says how often each was
given, `texts` and `numbers` hold a string or number flag's value,
`bools` a boolean's and `lists` a repeatable flag's values in the order
given. A flag that was not given
reads as `""`, `0`, `false` or no values; `has` tells that apart from one
given as such.

```ts
class ParsedFlags
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new ParsedFlags(table: FlagTable)` |  |
| `argument: string` |  |
| `bools: boolean[]` |  |
| `code: i32` |  |
| `command: string` |  |
| `commandAt: i32` |  |
| `counts: i32[]` |  |
| `lists: string[][]` |  |
| `message: string` |  |
| `numbers: f64[]` |  |
| `ok: boolean` |  |
| `positionals: string[]` |  |
| `table: FlagTable` |  |
| `texts: string[]` |  |
| `all(name: string): string[]` | Every value a repeatable flag was given, in order, as a fresh array; empty when it was not given. |
| `bool(name: string): boolean` | A boolean flag's value: true for `--name`, false for `--no-name` or when it was not given. |
| `exitUsage(): void` | The usage error on stderr, then exit status 2. On a parse that succeeded it panics: there is no error to report. |
| `fail(code: i32, message: string, argument: string): void` | Records the first usage error; a parse stops at it. |
| `has(name: string): boolean` | Whether the flag `name`, of any kind, was given at all (`--no-name` counts). |
| `num(name: string): f64` | A number flag's value, or `0` when it was not given. |
| `slot(name: string, kind: i32): i32` | The index of the flag `name` of `kind`; a name the table does not declare so is a bug, and panics. |
| `str(name: string): string` | A string flag's value, or `""` when it was not given. |
| `take(at: i32, flag: string, value: string, arg: string): void` | Stores `value` for the flag at `at`, spelled `flag` in `arg`, or fails as its kind requires. |
| `usageError(): string` | What `exitUsage` prints: `<program>: <message>` and the usage line, each ending in a newline. |
| `usageLine(): string` | The usage line the error's hint shows: the matched command's path and shape, or `<command>` when the table has commands and none matched, then `[flags]`. |

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_BOOLEAN: i32`

A flag that takes no value: `--name` is true and `--no-name` false, read with `bool`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_ERR_BOOLEAN_VALUE: i32`

`--name=value` (or `--no-name=value`) on a boolean.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_ERR_MISSING_VALUE: i32`

A flag that takes a value, last on the line with no `=`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_ERR_NOT_A_NUMBER: i32`

A number flag's value that is not one finite number.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_ERR_REPEATED: i32`

A flag that is not repeatable, given a second time (for a boolean, in either spelling).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_ERR_UNKNOWN: i32`

A `--name` the table does not declare, or a short option (`-v`), which the grammar does not have.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_ERR_UNKNOWN_COMMAND: i32`

Leading words that spell no declared command, when the table declares any.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_NUMBER: i32`

A flag whose one value is a number, read with `num`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_OK: i32`

`ParsedFlags.code` for a parse with no usage error.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_REPEATABLE: i32`

A flag that takes a value each time it is given, every one kept in order, read with `all`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`FLAG_STRING: i32`

A flag that takes one value, read with `str`.
